s: August 21, 2006 - I would use it when for example, I had to borrow something for a long time because I couldn't afford it, so when I finally buy it, I say: Now I bought myself (my own) skiis, so I do not need to borrow them anymore. I think that this "myself" introduces more a better description of a feeling that the speaker has towards something that he bought, than a simple meaning that serves only to understand what he had done. Ok, he bought a car. But he bought HIMSELF a car, the very one he wanted so long!
